Implementation Plan

# Implementation plan — isolate workflow-log analysis

**Planning ref:** `main` at `9800a21ebff1f5fd5279ab423522879c5b5165f4`. The clarification workflow asked no questions; `/answer [auto-answered-by-clarify]` confirms the reported security issue is the scope. No integration branch was specified, so no branch mismatch is established.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion  
Reuse-audit: extends `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` and its existing Docker/broker pattern  
Scope-mode justification: Fixing only the Codex call at line 1115 would leave the deep-audit, API-redundancy, weekly-retro, and consumer-retro Codex calls with the same trust boundary. Include those calls and their reporting paths, but do not redesign log collection. This is the complete security fix rather than a superficially smaller one: **Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed** (`unattended_system_instructions.md` §6).

## Automation and lifecycle

- **Existing operation extended:** `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml`; dispatch and the existing Monday `0 9 * * 1` schedule remain its entry points.
- **Supervisor / database gate:** Neither is needed. Isolation runs are short-lived; no database operation is introduced.
- **Removal registry:** Not applicable if the existing isolation helper is extended rather than adding a single-use or long-running script.

## Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml` — separate unprivileged analysis from authenticated publication for all four Codex paths.
- `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` and, only if its interface needs it, `scripts/clarify_openrouter_broker.py` — add a backward-compatible, bounded workflow-analysis profile; preserve existing clarify behavior.
- `scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh` — separate consumer narrative generation from its GitHub writes.
- `tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_failure_contract.py`, `tests/test_workflow_retro_fanout.py`, and the existing clarify-isolation contract tests — cover the new boundary and preserve old contracts.
- `agents.md` and a `changelog.d/6197-*.md` fragment — document the changed workflow boundary. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` directly.

## Modules and flow

1. Keep `scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py`’s collection behavior, including CI runs. Its `list_runs_for_repo` selects workflow families without a fork-origin exclusion; filtering forks alone would not make other collected logs trusted. GitHub’s run listing supplies run metadata, while the collector already fetches log archives—no new GitHub API lookup is needed for this fix. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10&utm_source=openai))
2. Extend the clarify isolation runner for explicitly allowed analysis roles. Reuse its fixed-destination host model broker, credential-free container, read-only source snapshot, and `--network none`; admit only bounded, regular-file prompt/log inputs and return only bounded output files. Preserve the existing clarify arguments and role validation. The provider key stays in the host broker; the agent receives neither it nor a GitHub token, checkout credential, host workspace, or arbitrary network route. Docker documents `none` as the network-isolated driver. ([docs.docker.com](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/none/?utm_source=openai))
3. Make the Codex portions of `analyze-commit-notify`, `deep-audit`, `api-redundancy`, and `weekly-retro` run in read-only, least-privilege model jobs. Keep their existing job IDs for the **publisher** jobs so downstream `needs`/status interfaces remain stable; add model-job predecessors that hand off validated text through same-run artifacts. Disable persisted checkout credentials in model jobs. GitHub supports artifacts for job-to-job transfer and job-scoped token permissions. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflow-artifacts?apiVersion=2022-11-28&utm_source=openai))
4. Move issue failure markers/labels, report commits and pushes, tracker comments, and Telegram reporting into publisher jobs. Publishers validate the artifact type, size, expected headings, and fixed report-path pattern before use; treat model prose as data, never shell source or a command. Preserve existing retry, failure-marker, no-activity, and report-filename behavior.
5. Split `workflow_retro_fanout.sh`’s per-consumer model invocation from its authenticated tracker upsert. Keep its current opt-out, no-activity, per-repo failure, and `WORKFLOW_RETRO_FANOUT_V1` behavior; do not leave a `danger-full-access` fallback in the publishing path.

## Data structures and API/interface changes

Keep `workflow_log_report.json`, report Markdown headings, tracker markers, workflow inputs, log prefixes, and existing publisher job outputs compatible. Add only internal, fixed-name model-result artifacts and their validated status/path handoff. No new endpoint or external service is proposed. Preserve the collector’s existing GitHub run/log API calls and the broker’s fixed provider destination. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?utm_source=openai))

## Decisions

### D1 — Isolate logs rather than exclude fork runs
- **Chosen:** Treat every collected log and derived summary as untrusted model input.
- **Alternatives considered:** Exclude fork-origin CI runs; change only the call cited at line 1115.
- **Why:** Either shortcut leaves other untrusted log sources or privileged Codex paths exposed.

### D2 — Reuse the existing isolation boundary
- **Chosen:** Extend the clarify container/broker mechanism with separately validated analysis roles and inputs.
- **Alternatives considered:** Rely on Codex’s host `read-only` sandbox or build a second provider broker.
- **Why:** The existing boundary keeps provider credentials outside the agent and restricts container networking; duplicating it increases security drift.

## Security considerations

The trust boundary is **GitHub log/archive → model prompt → model output → authenticated publisher**. Model jobs need no write authorization; publisher jobs retain only the permissions their existing GitHub writes require. Validate log-input paths and bounds before mounting, and output paths/content before publication. Reject symlinks, traversal, unexpected artifacts, oversized files, and malformed statuses. A fork PR’s log instruction to read credentials, invoke shell/network tools, or alter a publisher command must have no such capability. Do not echo untrusted model stderr or log text into workflow-command syntax. GitHub recommends treating untrusted workflow input carefully and limiting token permissions. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use?learn=getting_started&learnProduct=actions&utm_source=openai))

## Risks and edge cases

- **Failure handling:** A missing broker, Docker failure, absent artifact, or invalid output must stop publication and retain the applicable failure signal—not fall back to host Codex.
- **Compatibility:** Deep audit and API redundancy consume the preceding report; preserve that ordering and existing concurrent-push retry behavior. Consumer fan-out must still run when the source retro has no activity.
- **Issue/code conflict:** None found for the cited call: `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml:1115` is a `danger-full-access` Codex invocation. The same pattern also appears in the other analysis paths, which this plan includes.
- **Capacity:** Check `wc -c` after editing the workflow; it is currently below the repository’s 480,000-byte split threshold.

## Testing considerations

Extend the existing contract tests to assert every analysis Codex call uses isolation, no model job has write permission or persisted credentials, and only publisher jobs perform GitHub writes. Exercise injected CI-log instructions, missing/invalid/oversized artifacts, container failure without host fallback, report-path traversal, all four output contracts, and consumer no-activity/partial-failure behavior. Run the repository’s pinned lint and focused tests, then workflow syntax/size checks and the relevant CI suite; do not treat an unpinned global validator as authoritative.

## Pre-execution self-check

The plan covers the reported call and the equivalent model-to-privileged-host paths, names the scheduler and publisher handoffs, preserves existing external interfaces, and requires no missing scalar input. **No files were modified during planning.**
